---
title: Processing
description: From count tables to integrated data
order: 30
---

Processing takes the per-sample H5MU files produced during [ingestion](ingestion.qmd) and produces a clean, integrated dataset ready for downstream analysis. It covers quality control, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and batch correction.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-processing-overview
%%| fig-cap: Overview of the processing steps, from per-sample count tables to an integrated, clustered dataset.
flowchart LR
  h5mu["H5MU per sample"] --> single["Single-sample QC & filtering"]
  single --> concat["Concatenation"]
  concat --> multi["Multi-sample normalization & dim. reduction"]
  multi --> integration["Integration / batch correction"]
  integration --> out["Integrated H5MU"]
```

## Single-sample processing

Each sample is first processed independently to apply QC filters. The `rna_singlesample` workflow handles the following steps:

- QC metric calculation (counts, detected genes, mitochondrial fraction)
- Cell filtering based on counts and gene thresholds
- Doublet detection (Scrublet)

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/rna/rna_singlesample/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id sample_A \
  --input sample_A.h5mu \
  --output sample_A_processed.h5mu \
  --min_counts 500 \
  --max_counts 50000 \
  --min_genes_per_cell 200 \
  --var_name_mitochondrial_genes "mitochondrial" \
  --publish_dir results/
```

For CITE-seq (GEX + protein), use `prot_singlesample` in addition to `rna_singlesample` to apply protein-specific QC and CLR normalization to the `prot` modality.

Run single-sample processing across all samples using a parameter list:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/rna/rna_singlesample/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --param_list samples.csv \
  --publish_dir results/
```

See [Parameter lists](parameter_lists.qmd) for the `samples.csv` format.

## Multi-sample processing

Once all samples have been processed individually, they are concatenated and normalized together. The `rna_multisample` workflow performs:

- Concatenation of all per-sample H5MU files
- Log-normalization and log1p transformation
- Highly variable feature selection
- PCA
- Neighbor graph construction
- UMAP

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/rna/rna_multisample/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id cohort_01 \
  --input "results/sample_*.h5mu" \
  --output cohort_01_multisample.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

:::{.callout-tip}
The `process_samples` workflow combines `rna_singlesample` (per sample) and `rna_multisample` into a single convenience workflow, and `process_batches` adds a batching step for very large cohorts. See the [Components reference](../components/) for details.
:::

## Integration and batch correction

When samples come from multiple donors, batches, or sequencing runs, batch effects need to be corrected before clustering. OpenPipelines provides several integration workflows, all producing a corrected embedding that is then used for neighbor graph construction, Leiden clustering, and UMAP:

| Workflow | Method | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `harmony_leiden` | Harmony | Fast, embedding-based correction |
| `scvi_leiden` | scVI | Deep learning, handles complex batches |
| `scanorama_leiden` | Scanorama | Pan-datasets with partial overlap |
| `bbknn_leiden` | BBKNN | Batch-balanced neighbor graphs |
| `totalvi_leiden` | totalVI | Multiomics (RNA + protein) |

Example with Harmony:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/harmony_leiden/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id cohort_01 \
  --input cohort_01_multisample.h5mu \
  --obs_covariates "batch" \
  --output cohort_01_integrated.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

Example with scVI:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/scvi_leiden/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  --id cohort_01 \
  --input cohort_01_multisample.h5mu \
  --obs_batch "batch" \
  --output cohort_01_integrated.h5mu \
  --publish_dir results/
```

## Using a parameters file

For complex runs, store all parameters in a YAML file:

```yaml
# params.yaml
id: cohort_01
input: cohort_01_multisample.h5mu
output: cohort_01_integrated.h5mu
obs_covariates: "batch"
leiden_resolution: 1.0
```

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -main-script target/nextflow/workflows/integration/harmony_leiden/main.nf \
  -revision 4.0.3 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -params-file params.yaml \
  --publish_dir results/
```

## Output

The output is a single integrated H5MU file containing:

- Corrected cell embeddings in `.obsm` (e.g. `X_integrated`)
- Leiden cluster labels in `.obs`
- UMAP coordinates in `.obsm`

This file is the starting point for [downstream analysis](downstream.qmd) such as cell type annotation and differential expression.

See the [Components reference](../components/) for the full argument list of each processing and integration workflow.
